title: Claude Code 101: The workflow that changed how I build features | Robin Champsaur

facts.fact: In Claude Code, Plan Mode is toggled by pressing Shift + Tab twice.
facts.quote: Toggle it by pressing `Shift + Tab` twice. Describe the feature you want in detail.

facts.fact: The author says running /agents in Claude Code opens the interface for managing subagents.
facts.quote: Run `/agents` in Claude Code to open the management interface.

facts.fact: The author says project-level subagents are stored in .claude/agents/ and user-level subagents in ~/.claude/agents/.
facts.quote: create new agents at project level (stored in `.claude/agents/`) or user level (stored in `~/.claude/agents/`)

facts.fact: The author's example frontend subagent is configured with the tools Read, Edit, Bash, Grep, and Glob and the model sonnet.
facts.value: Read, Edit, Bash, Grep, Glob; model sonnet
facts.quote: tools: Read, Edit, Bash, Grep, Glob

facts.fact: The author states that each subagent operates in its own context window, which keeps the main conversation clean and focused.
facts.quote: Each subagent operates in its own context window, keeping your main conversation clean and focused.

facts.fact: The author recommends creating the claude.md file in the project root as a persistent guide that Claude references on almost every prompt.
facts.quote: set up a `claude.md` file in your project root.

facts.fact: The author lists three core elements for success with Claude Code: the claude.md file, Plan Mode, and specialized subagents.
facts.quote: Three elements make the difference between frustration and flow:

facts.fact: The author says that to have Claude invoke a subagent automatically when relevant, the subagent's description should include phrases like "Use proactively".
facts.quote: Include phrases like "Use proactively" if you want Claude to invoke it automatically when relevant.

facts.fact: The author's feature development pattern in Claude Code has six steps, starting with toggling Plan Mode using Shift + Tab.
The author recommends reviewing the claude.md project file weekly as the project evolves.
facts.quote: Your claude.md should too. Review it weekly.

facts.fact: The author advises resetting context between features because long conversations cause Claude to lose earlier context.
facts.quote: Long conversations cause Claude to lose earlier context. Clean slate, clean code.

facts.fact: With the Linear MCP integration configured, Claude can read ticket descriptions, update statuses, and create subtasks.
facts.quote: With Linear, Claude can read ticket descriptions, update statuses, and create subtasks.

facts.fact: The author lists four common mistakes to avoid when using Claude Code, including skipping the planning phase and accepting the first output.
